blocks.title: Causal (Look-Ahead) Mask
blocks.statement:
All entries with $j > i$ in the $T \times T = 4 \times 4$ score matrix $\mathbf{Z}$ are set to $-\infty$ before the softmax.

Therefore the attention weights become zero, $\alpha\left( \mathbf{q}_i, \mathbf{K},r \right)=0$ for all $r>i$.

Therefore, the weighted sum of values is restricted to positions up to and including $i$.

$$
\text{row}_i(\mathbf{A}) = \sum_{r=1}^{i} \alpha(\mathbf{q}_i, \mathbf{K}, r)\; \mathbf{v}_r^T
$$

This preserves the autoregressive property: position $i$ can only depend on positions $1, \ldots, i$.

blocks.title: FFN
blocks.statement:
$$
\text{FFN}(\mathbf{x}) = \phi\!\left(\mathbf{x}\mathbf{W}_1 + \mathbf{b}_1\right)\mathbf{W}_2 + \mathbf{b}_2
$$

$\phi$ is the activation function, $\mathbf{W}_1 : (D{=}512,\, D_{ff}{=}2048)$ and $\mathbf{W}_2 : (D_{ff}{=}2048,\, D{=}512)$. The original paper uses $\phi = \text{ReLU}$; in practice GELU is commonly preferred:

$$
\text{ReLU}(\mathbf{x}) = \max(0,\, \mathbf{x})
\qquad\qquad
\text{GELU}(\mathbf{x}) \approx \mathbf{x} \cdot \sigma(1.702\,\mathbf{x})
$$

blocks.title: Padding Mask
blocks.statement:
A padding mask zeros out attention for any padding token.

$\sigma \left( \mathbf{QK^T} \right)_{i,j}$ is set to zero whenever query $i$ or key $j$'s token correspond to padding. Usually this is done via setting $\mathbf{QK^T}_{i,j}$ to negative infinity.

Equivalently, $\sigma \left(\mathbf{Z}  \right)_{i,j} = \sigma \left( \frac{\mathbf{QK^T}}{\sqrt{D_k}} \right)_{i,j} = \alpha(\mathbf{q}_i, \mathbf{K}, j)=0$ when $i$ or $j$ represent padding.

blocks.title: Positional Encoding
blocks.statement:
Positional encodings $PE_{\text{src}} : (S{=}5,\, D{=}512)$ are added elementwise (not concatenated),
for each position
$s \in \left\{1,...,S \right\}$
and dimension index
$d \in \left\{ 1,\dots,D \right\}$ taking either $2i+1$ or $2i$

$$
PE_{\text{src}} :(S,D)  =
\begin{cases}
\begin{aligned}
PE_{\text{src}} \left[ s, 2i \right]
&=
\sin \left( \dfrac{s}{10,000^{\left(\dfrac{2i}{D}\right)}} \right)
\\\\
PE_{\text{src}} \left[ s, 2i+1 \right]
&=
\cos \left( \dfrac{s}{10,000^{\left(\dfrac{2i}{D}\right)}} \right)
\end{aligned}
\end{cases}
$$

blocks.title: Remark — what the cross-attention is comparing
blocks.statement:
The similarity $\mathbf{Z}_{i,j} = \mathbf{q}_i \cdot \mathbf{k}_j$ measures how much **target token $i$ attends to source token $j$**.

For example when generating $\mathbf{Y}_{\text{tgt}}$ every query representing $\mathbf{X}_{\text{tgt}}$ is allowed attend to all keys representing source $\mathbf{X}_{\text{tgt}}$

$$
\text{row}_i(\mathbf{A}) = \sum_{r=1}^{S} \alpha(\mathbf{q}_i, \mathbf{K}, r)\; \mathbf{v}_r^T
$$

For example when trying to generate $i=4$ target MAGNIFIQUE the query $\mathbf{q}_4$ for (shifted right target) EST is allowed to attend to all English states.

blocks.title: Remark — what the self-attention is comparing
blocks.statement:
Let's consider the first layer of the stack.

$$
\text{MHA}\!\left(\tilde{\mathbf{X}}_{\text{src}},\; \tilde{\mathbf{X}}_{\text{src}},\; \tilde{\mathbf{X}}_{\text{src}}\right) : (S{=}5,\, D{=}512)
$$

All three of $\mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{K}, \mathbf{V}$ are projections of the same matrix $\tilde{\mathbf{X}}_{\text{src}}$, so $\mathbf{Z}_{i,j} = \mathbf{q}_i \cdot \mathbf{k}_j$ measures how much **source token $i$ attends to source token $j$**. For example, token $i = \text{LOVELY}$ may learn to attend strongly to token $j = \text{TODAY}$, capturing their syntactic relationship. Output row $i$ is:

$$
\text{row}_i(\mathbf{A}) = \sum_{r=1}^{S} \alpha(\mathbf{q}_i, \mathbf{K}, r)\; \mathbf{v}_r^T
$$

a blend of all $S=5$ source value vectors, weighted by relevance to source position $i$.

blocks.title: Remark — training vs inference
blocks.statement: During training, all $T=4$ target tokens are processed **in parallel** by a single decoder call (with the causal mask enforcing causality). This is what makes training efficient. During inference, the decoder is called **sequentially** $T{+}1$ times — each step's output token becomes part of the next step's input — since the true targets are unknown. The causal mask and the shifted-right convention together ensure that training exactly mimics the conditional dependencies seen at inference time.

blocks.title: Remark — why shift right
blocks.statement: The shift means: the decoder at position $i$ must predict target token $i+1$ using only the tokens at positions $1, \ldots, i$. Seeing $\langle\text{BOS}\rangle$ it should predict LE; seeing $\langle\text{BOS}\rangle$, LE it should predict TEMPS; and so on. This is **teacher forcing** — the ground-truth tokens are fed in as input rather than the model's own previous predictions.

blocks.title: Remark — weight tying
blocks.statement: The paper shares the same weight matrix between the two embedding layers (source and target) and the pre-softmax linear transformation $\mathbf{W}_O$. In the embedding layers the weights are multiplied by $\sqrt{D}$.

blocks.title: Attention
blocks.statement:
$\text{Attention}: (T,D_k) \times (S,D_k) \times (S,D_v) \to (T,D_v)$ maps

$$
\text{Attention} \left( \mathbf{Q,K,V} \right) =
\sigma \left( \dfrac{\mathbf{Q K^T}}{\sqrt{D_k}} \right) \mathbf{V}
: (T,D_v)
$$

for row wise softmax $\sigma$

blocks.title: Multi Head Attention
blocks.statement:
Given sequence lengths $S, T \in \mathbb{N}$, dimension lengths $D_q, D_k, D_v, D \in \mathbb{N}$, $h\in \mathbb{N}$ that divides $D$ and parameters $\mathbf{W_i^Q, W_i^K, W_i^V}$, for $i=1,...,h$.

$\text{MultiHeadAttention}: (T,D_q) \times (S,D_k) \times (S,D_v) \to (T,D)$

$$
\begin{split}
\text{MultiHeadAttention} \left(\mathbf{Q,K,V}  \right) =
\left[ \mathbf{H_1},...,\mathbf{H_h} \right]
: (T,D)
\\ \\
\mathbf{H_i}
 \coloneqq
\text{Attention} \left( \mathbf{Q'_i}, \mathbf{K'_i}, \mathbf{V'_i} \right)
:(T,D_h)
\\ \\
\begin{array}{ccccc}
   \mathbf{Q'_i} &  = & \mathbf{Q} & \mathbf{W_i^Q} &:(T,D_h), \\
   & & (T,D_q) & (D_q,D_h) &
   \\ \\
   \mathbf{K'_i} &  = & \mathbf{K} & \mathbf{W_i^K} &:(S,D_h) \\
   & & (S,D_k) & (D_k,D_h) &
   \\ \\
   \mathbf{V'_i} &  = & \mathbf{V} & \mathbf{W_i^V} &:(S,D_h) \\
   & & (S,D_v) & (D_v,D_h) &
   \\
\end{array}
\\ i=1,...,h, \quad D_h \coloneqq \frac{D}{h}
\end{split}
$$

blocks.title: Notation
blocks.statement:
Let $(S, D)$ denote the shape $\mathbb{R}^{S \times D}$ and write $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{S \times D}$ as $\mathbf{X} : (S, D)$.

* $S, T$ denote sequence lengths (source and target respectively)
* $D$ denotes the model embedding dimension
* $D_k, D_v, D_q$ denote key, value, and query dimensions
* $h$ denotes the number of attention heads, with $D_h \coloneqq D/h$

blocks.title: Attention is permutation invariant
blocks.statement:
Notice that row $i$ of $\mathbf{A}$ is a function of $\mathbf{q_i, K,V}$,

$$
\text{row}_i \left( \mathbf{A} \right) =
\sum_{r=1}^S \alpha(\mathbf{q_i},\mathbf{K},r) \mathbf{v_r^T}
\eqqcolon f(\mathbf{q_i, K,V})
$$

Therefore if we permute two rows of $\mathbf{Q}$, the output of Attention has the same two rows of $\mathbf{A}$ permuted.

blocks.title: Borel Measurable Function
blocks.statement: Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}$. A function $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ is *Borel measurable* if $f^{-1}(B)$ is Borel for every Borel set $B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$.

blocks.title: Borel Set
blocks.statement:
The collection of *Borel subsets* of $\mathbb{R}$ is the smallest $\sigma$-algebra on $\mathbb{R}$ that contains all open subsets of $\mathbb{R}$.

A set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is *Borel* if $E$ is in this collection.

blocks.title: Lebesgue Measurable Set
blocks.statement:
A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is *Lebesgue measurable* if there exists a Borel set $B \in \mathcal{B}$ such that

$$
B \subseteq A
\quad \text{and} \quad
|A \setminus B| = 0.
$$

blocks.title: Lebesgue Measure
blocks.statement:
*Lebesgue measure* is outer measure restricted to the Borel measurable space:

$$
(\mathbb{R}, \mathcal{B}, \mu), \qquad \mu = |\cdot|.
$$

blocks.title: Measurable Function
blocks.statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{S})$ be a measurable space. A function $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ is *measurable* if

$$
f^{-1}(B) \in \mathcal{S}
$$

for every Borel set $B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$.

blocks.title: Measurable Space
blocks.statement: A *measurable space* $(X, \mathcal{S})$ is a set $X$ together with a $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{S}$ on $X$.

blocks.title: Measure
blocks.statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{S})$ be a measurable space. A function $\mu : \mathcal{S} \to [0, \infty]$ is a *measure* if:

**(i)** $\mu(\varnothing) = 0$.

**(ii)** For every disjoint sequence $\{E_k : k \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$,

$$
\mu\left(\bigcup_{k \in \mathbb{N}} E_k\right) = \sum_{k \in \mathbb{N}} \mu(E_k).
$$

blocks.title: Measure Space
blocks.statement: A *measure space* $(X, \mathcal{S}, \mu)$ consists of a set $X$, a $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{S}$ on $X$, and a measure $\mu$ on $(X, \mathcal{S})$.

blocks.title: Outer Measure
blocks.statement:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$. The *outer measure* of $A$ is

$$
|A| := \inf \left\{ \sum_{k \in \mathbb{N}} \ell(I_k) \ \middle|\
\begin{array}{l}
\bullet\ I_k \text{ is an open interval for all } k \in \mathbb{N}, \\
\bullet\ A \subseteq \bigcup_{k \in \mathbb{N}} I_k
\end{array}
\right\}.
$$

blocks.title: $\sigma$-Algebra
blocks.statement:
Let $X$ be a set and let $\mathcal{S}$ be a set of subsets of $X$. Then $\mathcal{S}$ is a *$\sigma$-algebra* on $X$ if:

**(i)** $\varnothing \in \mathcal{S}$.

**(ii)** If $E \in \mathcal{S}$, then $E^c = X \setminus E \in \mathcal{S}$.

**(iii)** If $\{E_k : k \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$, then

$$
\bigcup_{k \in \mathbb{N}} E_k \in \mathcal{S}.
$$

That is, $\mathcal{S}$ contains the empty set, is closed under complements, and is closed under countable unions.

blocks.title: Limit Point
blocks.statement: A *limit point* of a set $F \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a point $x \in \mathbb{R}$ such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $y \in F$ with $0 < |x - y| < \varepsilon$. A set is closed if and only if it contains all its limit points (Supplement for MIRA).

blocks.title: The fundamental axiom of analysis
blocks.statement:
If $a_{n} \in \mathbb{R}$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $A \in \mathbb{R}$

* $a_{1}\leq a_{2}\leq a_{3} \leq \dots$
* $a_n < A$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$

Then there exists $a \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $a_n \to a$ as $n \to ∞ $

blocks.title: Cauchy Sequence
blocks.statement: (CTA, Definition 4.66) A sequence $\mathbf{x}_n \in \mathbb{R}^m$ is a *Cauchy sequence* if, given $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $n_0(\varepsilon)$ such that $\|\mathbf{x}_p - \mathbf{x}_q\| < \varepsilon$ for all $p, q \geq n_0(\varepsilon)$.

blocks.title: Closed Set in $\mathbb{R}^m$
blocks.statement: (CTA, Definition 4.15) A set $F \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ is *closed* if whenever $\mathbf{x}_n \in F$ for each $n$ and $\mathbf{x}_n \to \mathbf{x}$ as $n \to \infty$, then $\mathbf{x} \in F$.

blocks.title: Continuity
blocks.statement: (CTA, Definition 1.12) Suppose $E \subseteq \mathbb{F}$ (an ordered field) and $f : E \to \mathbb{F}$. We say $f$ is *continuous* at $x \in E$ if, given any $\varepsilon > 0$, we can find $\delta_0(\varepsilon, x) > 0$ such that $|f(x) - f(y)| < \varepsilon$ for all $y \in E$ with $|x - y| < \delta_0(\varepsilon, x)$.

blocks.title: Continuity in $\mathbb{R}^m$
blocks.statement: (CTA, Definition 4.28) $f : E \to \mathbb{R}^p$ (where $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$) is *continuous* at $\mathbf{x} \in E$ if, given $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $\delta(\varepsilon, \mathbf{x}) > 0$ such that $\|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\| < \delta$ implies $\|f(\mathbf{x}) - f(\mathbf{y})\| < \varepsilon$.

blocks.title: Derivative (One-Dimensional)
blocks.statement:
(CTA, Definition 1.43) Let $U$ be an open set in $\mathbb{R}$. We say $f : U \to \mathbb{R}$ is *differentiable* at $t \in U$ with derivative $f'(t)$ if, given $\varepsilon > 0$, we can find $\delta(t, \varepsilon) > 0$ such that $(t - \delta, t + \delta) \subseteq U$ and

$$
\left| \frac{f(t+h) - f(t)}{h} - f'(t) \right| < \varepsilon
$$

whenever $0 < |h| < \delta(t, \varepsilon)$.

blocks.title: Differentiability in $\mathbb{R}^m$
blocks.statement:
(CTA, Definition 6.4) Let $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ with $B(\mathbf{x}, \delta) \subseteq E$ for some $\delta > 0$. We say $f : E \to \mathbb{R}^p$ is *differentiable* at $\mathbf{x}$ if there exists a linear map $\alpha : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^p$ such that

$$
f(\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{h}) = f(\mathbf{x}) + \alpha\mathbf{h} + \varepsilon(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{h})\|\mathbf{h}\|
$$

where $\|\varepsilon(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{h})\| \to 0$ as $\|\mathbf{h}\| \to 0$. We write $\alpha = Df(\mathbf{x})$.

blocks.title: Divergence to Infinity
blocks.statement: (CTA, Definition 1.27) We say $a_n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$ if, given any real $K$, we can find an $n_0(K)$ such that $a_n > K$ for all $n \geq n_0(K)$.

blocks.title: Limit of a Sequence
blocks.statement: (CTA, Definition 1.5) We say $a_n \to a$ as $n \to \infty$ if, given any $\varepsilon > 0$, we can find an integer $n_0(\varepsilon)$ such that $|a_n - a| < \varepsilon$ for all $n \geq n_0(\varepsilon)$.

blocks.title: lim sup
blocks.statement:
(CTA, Definition 3.23) If $x_n$ is a sequence bounded above,

$$
\limsup_{n \to \infty} x_n = \lim_{n \to \infty} \sup\{x_m : m \geq n\}.
$$

blocks.title: Norm and Inner Product on $\mathbb{R}^m$
blocks.statement: (CTA, §4.1) For $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^m$, the *Euclidean norm* is $\|\mathbf{x}\| = (\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{x})^{1/2}$, where $\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{y} = \sum_{j=1}^m x_j y_j$.

blocks.title: Operator Norm
blocks.statement: (CTA, Definition 6.13) If $\alpha : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^p$ is a linear map, then $\|\alpha\| = \sup_{\|\mathbf{x}\| \leq 1} \|\alpha\mathbf{x}\|$.

blocks.title: Open Set in $\mathbb{R}^m$
blocks.statement: (CTA, Definition 4.18) A set $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ is *open* if, whenever $\mathbf{x} \in U$, there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $\|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\| < \varepsilon$ implies $\mathbf{y} \in U$.

blocks.title: Supremum (Least Upper Bound)
blocks.statement: (CTA, Definition 3.3) For a non-empty set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, $\alpha$ is a *least upper bound* (supremum) for $A$ if: (i) $\alpha \geq a$ for all $a \in A$; (ii) if $\beta \geq a$ for all $a \in A$, then $\beta \geq \alpha$.

blocks.title: Uniform Continuity
blocks.statement: (CTA, Definition 4.60) $f : E \to \mathbb{R}^p$ is *uniformly continuous* on $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ if, given $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $\delta(\varepsilon) > 0$ such that $\|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\| < \delta$ implies $\|f(\mathbf{x}) - f(\mathbf{y})\| < \varepsilon$ for all $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \in E$.

blocks.title: Bolzano–Weierstrass Theorem
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 3.17) If $x_n \in \mathbb{R}$ and there exists $K$ with $|x_n| \leq K$ for all $n$, then we can find $n(1) < n(2) < \cdots$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $x_{n(j)} \to x$ as $j \to \infty$.

blocks.title: Bolzano–Weierstrass in $\mathbb{R}^m$
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 4.12) If $\mathbf{x}_n \in \mathbb{R}^m$ and $\|\mathbf{x}_n\| \leq K$ for all $n$, then there exist $n(1) < n(2) < \cdots$ and $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^m$ such that $\mathbf{x}_{n(j)} \to \mathbf{x}$ as $j \to \infty$.

blocks.title: General Principle of Convergence
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 4.70) A sequence in $\mathbb{R}^m$ converges if and only if it is a Cauchy sequence.

blocks.title: Chain Rule
blocks.statement: (CTA, Lemma 6.19) Let $f : U \to V$ be differentiable at $\mathbf{x}$ with derivative $\alpha$, and $g : V \to \mathbb{R}^q$ differentiable at $\mathbf{y} = f(\mathbf{x})$ with derivative $\beta$. Then $g \circ f$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x}$ with derivative $\beta\alpha$, i.e., $D(g \circ f)(\mathbf{x}) = Dg(f(\mathbf{x})) \cdot Df(\mathbf{x})$.

blocks.title: Continuous Image of Closed Bounded Set
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 4.41) If $K$ is a closed bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^m$ and $f : K \to \mathbb{R}^p$ is continuous, then $f(K)$ is closed and bounded.

blocks.title: Cauchy–Schwarz Inequality
blocks.statement: (CTA, Lemma 4.2) For $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \in \mathbb{R}^m$, $|\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{y}| \leq \|\mathbf{x}\|\|\mathbf{y}\|$.

blocks.title: Constant Value Theorem
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 1.46) If $f : U \to \mathbb{R}$ is differentiable with $f'(t) = 0$ for all $t \in U$ (where $U$ is an open interval or $\mathbb{R}$), then $f$ is constant.

blocks.title: Extreme Value Theorem
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 4.44) If $K$ is a closed bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^m$ and $f : K \to \mathbb{R}$ is continuous, then there exist $\mathbf{k}_1, \mathbf{k}_2 \in K$ such that $f(\mathbf{k}_2) \leq f(\mathbf{k}) \leq f(\mathbf{k}_1)$ for all $\mathbf{k} \in K$.

blocks.title: Intermediate Value Theorem
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 1.35) If $f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ is continuous and $f(a) > 0 > f(b)$, then there exists $c \in [a, b]$ such that $f(c) = 0$.

blocks.title: Mean Value Inequality
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 1.42) Let $U = (\alpha, \beta)$. If $f : U \to \mathbb{R}$ is differentiable with $f'(t) \leq K$ for all $t \in U$, and $a, b \in U$ with $b > a$, then $f(b) - f(a) \leq (b - a)K$.

blocks.title: Mean Value Inequality (Higher Dimensions)
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 6.27) If $f : U \to \mathbb{R}^p$ is differentiable on an open set $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$, and the line segment $L$ joining $\mathbf{a}$ to $\mathbf{b}$ lies entirely in $U$ with $\|Df(\mathbf{x})\| \leq K$ for all $\mathbf{x} \in L$, then $\|f(\mathbf{a}) - f(\mathbf{b})\| \leq K\|\mathbf{a} - \mathbf{b}\|$.

blocks.title: Mean Value Theorem
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 4.49) If $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ is continuous with $f$ differentiable on $(a,b)$, then there exists $c \in (a,b)$ such that $f(b) - f(a) = (b-a)f'(c)$.

blocks.title: Rolle's Theorem
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 4.52) If $g : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ is continuous, differentiable on $(a,b)$, and $g(a) = g(b)$, then there exists $c \in (a,b)$ such that $g'(c) = 0$.

blocks.title: Supremum Principle
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 3.7) Every non-empty set of real numbers bounded above has a supremum.

blocks.title: Uniform Continuity on Closed Bounded Sets
blocks.statement: (CTA, Theorem 4.63) If $K$ is a closed bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^m$ and $f : K \to \mathbb{R}^p$ is continuous, then $f$ is uniformly continuous on $K$.

blocks.title: Stars and Bars
blocks.statement:
For fixed $n,k \in \mathbb{N}$,

$$
\left|
\left\{
(x_1,\dots,x_k)
\;\middle|\;
\sum_{i=1}^{k} x_i = n,\ 0 \leq x_i \leq n
\right\}
\right|
=
\binom{n+k-1}{k-1}.
$$

blocks.title: Shapley Value
Shapley Formula
blocks.statement:
$$
\phi_i(v)
= \sum_{S \subseteq N \setminus \{i\}}
\frac{|S|!\,(n-|S|-1)!}{n!}
\left(
v\!\left(S \cup \{i\}\right) - v(S)
\right)
$$

blocks.title: M inverse via Schur Complement of D
OLS
blocks.statement:
An ordinary least squares linear model (OLM) provides an estimate $\hat{\beta}$ of unknown coefficent $\beta \in \mathbb{R^{p \times 1}}$ to the problem,

$$
\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{X} \beta + \mathbf{\varepsilon}
$$

that minimises $\| \hat{\varepsilon} \|$ for $\hat{\varepsilon} = \mathbf{y-X \hat{\beta}}$.

Items $\mathbf{y} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times 1}, \mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R^{n \times p}}$ are known.

We **assume** that $\dfrac{\varepsilon}{\sigma}$ is
standard normal ([Definition](#def-standard_normal))
$\Leftrightarrow \varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0, \sigma^2 I_n})$,
where we may not know $\sigma$.

blocks.title: Coefficient of Determination
blocks.statement:
Given real and predicted $\mathbf{y}$, $\mathbf{\hat{y}}$, the **coefficent of determination** is defined as $R2(\mathbf{y,\hat{y}})$

$$
\begin{align*}
&
R2(\mathbf{y,\hat{y}}) = 1 - \frac{SS_{res}}{SS_{tot}},
& \text{for }
SS_{res} &= \| \mathbf{y-\hat{y}} \|^2
&
SS_{tot} &= \| \mathbf{y-\bar{y}} \|^2
\\
&&&=
\|\varepsilon\|^2
&&=
\mathbf{\|P_{1^\perp} y\|^2}
\end{align*}
$$

blocks.title: Sample Correlation
blocks.statement:
The **sample correlation** between vectors $\mathbf{x,y}$ is defined as

$$
\begin{align*}
r(\mathbf{x,y})
&=
\cfrac{\sum_i (x_i - \bar{x})(y_i - \bar{y})}{ \sqrt{\sum_i (x_i - \bar{x})^2}  \sqrt{\sum_i (y_i - \bar{y})^2}}
\\ &=
\cfrac{(\mathbf{x-P_1 x})^T (\mathbf{y-P_1 y})}{\| \mathbf{x-P_1 x} \| \| \mathbf{y-P_1 y} \|}
\\ &=
\bigg\langle
  \cfrac{\mathbf{P_{1^\perp} x}}{\|\mathbf{P_{1^\perp} x}\|},
  \cfrac{\mathbf{P_{1^\perp} y}}{\|\mathbf{P_{1^\perp} y}\|}
\bigg\rangle
\end{align*}
$$

Where we are lax with notation and let $\mathbf{1}$ denote $\text{span}\lbrace\mathbf{1}\rbrace$ for
$\mathbf{1} = [1,\ ...\ ,1]^T$.

blocks.title: Standard Normal Vector
blocks.statement:
A random vector $\mathbf{z} \in \mathbb{R^n}$ is standard normal **iff** components
$(\mathbf{z_i})_{i=1}^n$
are independantly identically distributed $\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0,I_n})$.

blocks.title: R² as Squared Correlation
blocks.statement:
If the predictions $\mathbf{\hat{y}}$ are standard ols as in [Definition](#def-ols_lm), then it holds that

$$
r(\mathbf{y}, \mathbf{\hat{y}}) = R2(\mathbf{y,\hat{y}})
$$

blocks.title: Remark
blocks.statement: Note that $\mathbf{\hat{y}}$ in [Definition](#def-R2) is general. We will specify details to prove the following.

blocks.title: ANOVA F-test
blocks.statement:
Let $p=p_0+p_1, \mathbf{X = [X_0, X_1]} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p}$ for
$\mathbf{X_0} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p_0}, \mathbf{X_1} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p_1}$

Consider the following two hypothesis of a full model vs a submodel,

$$
\begin{align*}
\textbf{H}_0 \text{ (null)}&:
\mathbf{y = X_0 \beta_\mathcal{N} + \varepsilon},
\quad
&& \mathbf{\beta}_\mathcal{N} \in \mathbb{R}^{p_0 \times 1},
\quad
&&&\mathbf{\varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0,I_n)}
\\
\textbf{H}_1 \text{ (full)}&:
\mathbf{y = X \beta_\mathcal{F} + \varepsilon},
\quad
&& \mathbf{\beta}_\mathcal{F} \in \mathbb{R}^{p \times 1},
\quad
&&&\mathbf{\varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0,I_n)}
\end{align*}
$$

Under the null hypothesis the following statistic is F distributed.

$$
\dfrac{\| \mathbf{\hat{\varepsilon}_\mathcal{N} - \hat{\varepsilon}_\mathcal{F}} \| /p_1}
{\| \mathbf{\hat{\varepsilon}_\mathcal{F}} \|/(n-p)}
\sim
F_{p_1, n-p}
$$

blocks.title: Solution of OLS
blocks.statement:
Assume that $\mathbf{X}$ has full rank.

The solution of OLS is given by $\hat{\beta} = \mathbf{(X^TX)^{-1}X^Ty}$.

blocks.title: Visit Counter
blocks.statement: Let $V_j = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \mathbf{1}_{\{X_n = j\}}$ be the total number of visits to state $j$.

blocks.title: Fundamental Matrix is the expected number of visits
blocks.statement:
$$
N_{i,j} = \mathbb{E}_i(V_j),
$$

i.e. $N_{i,j}$ is the expected number of visits to transient state $j$ when starting from transient state $i$.

blocks.title: Absorption Probability
blocks.statement:
Let $i$ be a transient state and $k$ an absorbing state. The probability of being absorbed into the recurrent class of $k$ (via state $k$) is

$$
\mathbb{P}_i(\text{absorbed by } k) = (NR)_{i,k}.
$$

blocks.title: Beta-Binomial Distribution
blocks.statement:
A random variable $X$ has a Beta-Binomial distribution, $X \sim \mathrm{BetaBin} (n,\alpha ,\beta)$ iff

$$
\mathbb{P}(X=x) = f(x|n,\alpha ,\beta) = {n \choose x} \Gamma(x+\alpha) \Gamma(n-x + \beta)
$$

for $x \in \lbrace 1,...,n \rbrace$.

blocks.title: Hypergeometric Distribution
blocks.statement:
Suppose there are $N$ balls, $X$ of the balls are red. Suppose we sample $M$ balls without replacement. Let $Y$ denote the number of red balls in the sample. Then,

$$
\mathbb{P}(Y=y) = \frac{{x \choose y} {N-X \choose M-y}}{N \choose M}
$$

blocks.title: Remark
blocks.statement: Note that $f(x|n,\alpha ,\beta) \propto \frac{1}{x! (n-x)!} \Gamma(x+\alpha) \Gamma(n-x + \beta)$ when we consider $x$ to be the only variable.

blocks.title: Hypergeometric Conjugate Prior
blocks.statement:
Suppose there are $N$ ballots and we sample $M \in \lbrace 1, ..., N \rbrace$. Let the random variable $X$ be the total number of Labour ballots. Let $Y$ be the number of Labour ballots in the sample.

If we place the following prior on $X$,

$$
p(x) = f(x|N,\alpha ,\beta)
$$

then likelihood of $Y$ given $X$ is hypergeometric and the posterior distribution of $X$ is given by

$$
p(x|y) = f(x-y|N-M, \alpha+y, \beta + M-y)
$$

blocks.title: Multivariate Normal
blocks.statement:
$\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is Multivariate Normal

$\iff \mathbf{x} \sim \mathcal{N} \mathbf{ \left( \mu, \Sigma \right) }$

$\iff$
There exists $\mathbf{\mu} \in \mathbb{R}^n, \mathbf{A} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times l}$
such that $\mathbf{x = Az + \mu}$ where $\mathbf{A^\top A = \Sigma}$.

Where $\mathbf{z} \in \mathbb{R}^l, l\leq n$ is a [standard normal vector](../linear_models/linear_models.md#def-standard_normal).

blocks.title: Conditional Gaussian
blocks.statement:
Let

$$
\mathbf{x} =
\begin{bmatrix}
\mathbf{x}_1\\
\mathbf{x}_2
\end{bmatrix}
\sim
\mathcal{N}
\left(
\begin{bmatrix}
\mathbf{\mu}_1\\
\mathbf{\mu}_2
\end{bmatrix},
\begin{bmatrix}
\mathbf{\Sigma}_{11} & \mathbf{\Sigma}_{12}\\
\mathbf{\Sigma}_{21} & \mathbf{\Sigma}_{22}
\end{bmatrix}
\right),
$$

where $\mathbf{\Sigma}$ is strictly positive definite. Define

$$
\mathbf{S}
:=
\mathbf{\Sigma}_{11} -
\mathbf{\Sigma}_{12}\mathbf{\Sigma}_{22}^{-1}\mathbf{\Sigma}_{21}.
$$

Then

$$
\mathbf{x}_1 \mid \mathbf{x}_2
\sim
\mathcal{N}
\left(
\mathbf{\mu}_1
+
\mathbf{\Sigma}_{12}\mathbf{\Sigma}_{22}^{-1}
\left(\mathbf{x}_2-\mathbf{\mu}_2\right),
\mathbf{S}
\right).
$$

blocks.title: Complete The Matrix Square
Multivariate PDF
blocks.statement:
Let $\mathbf{x} \sim \mathcal{N} \mathbf{ \left( \mu, \Sigma \right) }$
([Definition](#def-mv-normal)) with $\mathbf{\Sigma}$ (strictly) positive
definite. Then $\mathbf{x}$ has probability density function

$$
f_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{x})
=
\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{n/2} \, |\mathbf{\Sigma}|^{1/2}}
\exp \left(
-\frac{1}{2}
\mathbf{ (x-\mu)^\top \Sigma^{-1} (x-\mu) }
\right).
$$

blocks.title: Algebraic Theory
blocks.statement: An Algebraic Theory $T=(\Omega, E)$ is an operational type $(\Omega, \alpha)$ and set $E$ of equations in $\Omega$

blocks.title: Derived Equations
blocks.statement:
Let $E$ be a set of equations. The set $\tilde{E}$ of derived equation satisfies:

1. $E \subset \tilde{E}$

2. $\tilde{E}$ defines an equivalence relation $s \sim_E t \iff (s=t) \in \tilde{E}$ on the set of terms $F_{\Omega}(X)$

   1. reflexive: $(t=t) \in \tilde{E} \ \forall t \in F_{\Omega}(X)$
   2. symmetric: $(s=t) \implies (t=s)$
   3. transitive: $(s=t),(t=u) \implies (s=u)$

3. Substitution rules:

   1. $(s=t) \in \tilde{E} \implies (s[u / x_i] = t[u / x_i])$
   2. $(s=t), u \in F_{\Omega}(X_n) \implies u[s/x_i] = u[t/x_i]$

blocks.title: Derived Operations
blocks.statement:
Let $X_n= \lbrace x_1,...,x_n \rbrace$, $t \in F_{\Omega}(X_n)$, $A$ be a $\Omega$ structure.

The n-ary derived operation corresponding to $t \in F_{\Omega}(X)$, $t_A : A^n \rightarrow A$ is defined as

$\forall \underline{a} \in A^n$

$$
t_A(\underline{a})
= \begin{cases}
    a_i &\text{if } t = x_i \in X_n \\
    \omega_A \lparen t_1(\underline{a}) ,..., t_m(\underline{a}) \rparen
    &\text{if } t = \omega t_1 ... t_m, \text{ for } t_1,...,t_m \in F_{\Omega}(X_n), \alpha(\omega)=m
\end{cases}
$$

blocks.title: Finary Operation
blocks.statement: A finary operation is a map from $G$ to $G^n, n \in \left\{ 0, 1, 2, \dots \right\}$

blocks.title: function
blocks.statement:
A function $f: A\to B$ is

$$
f = \left\{ \left( a, f \left( a \right) \right): a \in A \right\}
$$

blocks.title: Homomorphism
blocks.statement:
A map $f:A\mapsto B$ is a homomorphism of $\Omega$ structures $A$ & $B$ if

$$
f(\omega_A (a_1,..., a_n)) = \omega_B (f(a_1),...,f(a_n))
$$

where $\alpha(\omega)=n$ and $\forall a_1,...,a_n \in A$

blocks.title: Model
blocks.statement: A model for an Algebraic Theory $T=(\Omega, E)$ or T-algebra is an Operational Structure $\Omega$ where all equations in $E$ are satisfied.

blocks.title: $n$-tuple
blocks.statement: An $n$-tuple is a map from $n$ to $A$

blocks.title: n-ary Equation
blocks.statement: An n-ary equation in operational type $(\Omega, \alpha)$ is an expression $(s=t)$ for $s,t \in F_{\Omega}(X_n)$

blocks.title: Satisfied
blocks.statement: An n-ary equation is satisfied in operational structure A iff $t_A \equiv s_A$

blocks.title: Operational Structure
blocks.statement:
An operational structure $(\Omega, \alpha)$ is

* a set $A$ with an operational type $(\Omega, \alpha)$

* a function $\omega_A : A^{\alpha(\omega)} \mapsto A$ for each $\omega \in \Omega$

$\omega_A$ is *the interpretation of abstract symbol* $\omega$ *in the structure $A$*.

blocks.title: Operational Type
blocks.statement:
An operational type is a pair $(\Omega, \alpha)$ with

* set of operation symbols $\Omega$
* a map
  $\alpha : \Omega \mapsto \mathbb{N}$ that assigns each $\omega \in \Omega$ it's arity $\alpha(\omega)$.

blocks.title: Ordered Pair
blocks.statement: $(a,b) \coloneqq \left\{ \left\{ a \right\}, \left\{ a, b \right\} \right\}$

blocks.title: $A^B$
The set of $\Omega$-terms in $X$
blocks.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an opertaional type and $X$ be a set.

The set $F_{\Omega}(X)$  of $\Omega$ terms is defined inductively:

1. If $x \in X$ then $x \in F_{Ω}(X)$
2. If $w \in \Omega$ with $\alpha(w)=n$ and $t_1,...,t_n \in \Omega$ then $wt_1...t_n \in F_{Ω}(X)$.

blocks.title: Equivalence Classes of Equations on X
blocks.statement: The equivalence classes of $\sim_E$ on $F_{\Omega}(X)$ is $F_{(\Omega, E)}(X)$

blocks.title: Group Theory Example
blocks.statement:
1. $t = m e x_1 = x_1 = s \in \tilde{E} \implies m e u = u \forall u \in F_{\Omega}(X)$
2. $u = m x_1 x_2$, $t=s$ as before, $\implies m x_1 \textcolor{red}{mex_1} = m x_1 \textcolor{red}{x_1}$

blocks.title: Group Theory Model
blocks.statement:
A group $G$ is a $\left( \Omega, E \right)$ model where $\Omega = \{ m,i,e\}$ and

$$
E=\{(m x_1 m x_2 x_3 = m m x_1 x_2 x_3), (mex_1=x_1), (m i x_1 x_1 = e)\}
$$

blocks.title: Group Operations
blocks.statement:
A group has associativity, identity and inverses.

$$
\begin{align*}
m &: G \times G & \to G & \text{ multiplication} \\
i &: G & \to G & \text{ inverse} \\
e &: G^0 = \left\{ \emptyset \right\} & \to G & \text{ identity}
\end{align*}
$$

Because $e(\emptyset) \in G$ picks a single element we usually denote it as $e$.

The standard group properties of associative, identity and inverse hold:

$$
\begin{align*}
m(x, m(y,z)) &= m(m(x,y),z) \\
m(e, x) &= x \\
m(i(x),x) &= e
\end{align*}
$$

For all $x,y,z \in G$.

blocks.title: Group Arity
blocks.statement: The operation symbols for a group make an operational type with $\Omega = \left\{ m,i,e \right\}$ and $\alpha(m)=2, \alpha(i)=1, \alpha(e)=0$

blocks.title: Nullary Set
blocks.statement:
$A^0$ is the set of maps from $0 = ∅ = \left\{  \right\}$ to $A$

The only map that does this is

$$
f = \left\{ (x, f(x)) : x \in \emptyset \right\} = \left\{  \right\}
$$

Hence $A^0$ = $\left\{ \emptyset \right\}$.

blocks.title: Derived Operations are literally themselves
blocks.statement:
If $t=mx_1 m x_2 x_3$ then $t_A(\underline{a})= m \left( a_1, m \left( a_2, a_3) \right) \right)$

More generally if
$t = \dots \omega x_1 \dots x_m \dots$ then
$t_A(\underline{a}) = \left( \dots, \omega \left( a_1, \dots a_m \right), \dots \right)$

In particular when $t \in A = F_{\Omega}(X_n)$, $\underline{u}=\left( u_1,\dots, u_n \right)$

$$
t_A(\underline{u}) =  \dots \omega u_1 \dots u_n \dots =
t[u_1/x_1, \dots, u_n/x_n] \ \forall \underline{u} \in F_{\Omega}(X_n)
$$

Where $t[u / x_i]$ denote replacing symbol $x_i$ with $u$ where $x_i$ appears in $t$.

This also means that

$$
t_{F_{\Omega}(X)}(x_1,\dots, x_n) = t
$$

blocks.title: Traditional Tuple
blocks.statement:
The tuple traditionally written as $\left( a,b,c \right)$ is

$\left\{ (0,a), (1,b), (2,c) \right\}$.

blocks.title: X terms from finite
blocks.statement: $F_{\Omega}(X)=\bigcup \lbrace F_{\Omega}(X^\prime) \mid X^\prime \subset X \text{ is finite} \rbrace$

blocks.title: $F_\Omega(X)$ is a sigma structure
blocks.statement:
1. The set of $\Omega$-terms in $X$, $F_{\Omega}(X)$ has a $\Omega$ structure.
2. Given any $\Omega$ structure $F_\Omega(X)$ and any map $f:X \mapsto A$ there exists a unique homomorphism $\hat{f}:F_\Omega(X) \mapsto A$

In other words $F_\Omega(X)$ is the free structure generated by $X$

blocks.title: The set of equivalence classes satisfies the equations in E
blocks.statement:
1. $F_{(\Omega, E)}(X)$ inherits $\Omega$-structure from $F_{\Omega}(X)$ and satisfies the equations in $E$.

2. $F_{(\Omega, E)}(X)$ is the free model generated by X.

   i.e. For any homomorphism $f: X \to (\Omega, E) \text{ model } A$ there is a unique homomorphism $\tilde{f}: F_{(\Omega, E)}(X) \to A$
